editorial:
Set on a sprawling Montana ranch in the 1920s, this slow-burn drama follows Phil Burbank, a sharp-tongued cowboy who rules his land and his brother with an iron grip. When his brother brings home a new wife and her quiet teenage son, Phil turns their lives into a daily battle of nerves. The tension builds slowly, like a storm rolling across the plains, and you never quite know when it will break. The movie looks gorgeous, with wide open landscapes that feel both beautiful and lonely.

The acting is the real star here. Every glance and silence carries weight, and the performances feel raw and real. The pacing is slow, so if you want fast action, this might test your patience. But if you enjoy layered characters and stories that reward your attention, you will be pulled in.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Phil's carefully built world falls apart. After bonding with the teen over braiding rope, Phil cuts his hand and later dies from an infection. The twist is that the teen had secretly rubbed the rope with anthrax from a dead cow, knowing Phil would handle it. The teen watches Phil's funeral from a window, calm and unbothered, while his mother and uncle celebrate their new life. It is a quiet, chilling ending that reveals the teen was the real predator all along.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character-driven dramas and westerns.
